<reason>A won by making the live clash decidable: after B conceded that routine papers and climate-model code can be openly licensed and that open licenses have a friction advantage, A showed B’s counterexamples already sit inside the motion’s exceptions, while post-grant enclosure is the error that actually leaves later labs waiting. B’s sharing-plan alternative was a real third way, not secrecy, and irreversibility of over-permission remained a residual risk, but it never justified rejecting a default for the bulk of funded papers, methods, and pipelines.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Q1/Q2 pressure on ordinary outputs and post-grant conversion, then A’s R2/closing classification of B’s examples as already-excepted hard cases rather than a reason to flip the default.</best_rebuttal>
